why: specs/03 §15.3. kb-samples/MANIFEST.md §Licence 3 asserts that no producer contact name, signatory or insured principal in this corpus is a real private individual. This file is what turns that assurance into a test: tests/extract/redacted-names.test.ts asserts that none of these strings appears in any prompt, any UI string, any help article, any marketing copy, any eval report or anywhere else in the repository outside tests/fixtures/coi/. The fixtures themselves are private test fixtures and are the one place these strings are allowed to be.
scope: Every producer.contact_name value in every expected-value file, plus every other personal name found anywhere in the corpus while labelling — including the ones that are documented placeholders. The rule is mechanical: it does not ask whether a name is real, because the point is that no name from this corpus can reach a customer-facing surface by accident.

provenance.name: John Burkart
provenance.status: REAL INDIVIDUAL. Found at labelling and reported here, which is what kb-samples/MANIFEST.md rule 4 asks the labeller to do: this settles C2's UNVERIFIED status. The signature is an image, it is not extracted as a value, and authorized_representative_present records only that the box is signed. The fixture is kept: it is a public document and the only genuinely issued certificate in the corpus.
